outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a support assembly for a coil spring, in particular for use in a vehicle suspension system or another arrangement in which a spring must be securely seated and vibrations transmitted through the spring are to be damped. The support assembly comprises an annular receiving element configured to receive and support an end region of the coil spring. A substantially disk-shaped damping element is connected to the receiving element and is positioned so that at least part of the spring bears against it during use.

The damping element includes an inner collar surrounding a central opening. This inner collar is bent or formed in the direction of the coil spring and may extend into, or adjacent to, the interior of the spring. The collar helps locate the spring relative to the support assembly and increases the contact area between the damping element and the receiving element. In this way, the damping element can reduce the transmission of vibration, impact, and structure-borne noise while also contributing to stable and reliable positioning of the spring.

The support assembly is manufactured by first placing the prefabricated damping element in a mold. The receiving element is then formed directly on the damping element by a molding or injection-molding process. During this operation, the material of the receiving element comes into direct contact with selected surfaces of the damping element, including, where appropriate, the bent inner collar. After curing or solidification, the receiving element and the damping element form an integrated structural unit.

This manufacturing method eliminates the need for a separate fastening operation and reduces the risk that the damping element will shift, detach, or be incorrectly positioned during assembly or operation. The direct molded connection also permits the two elements to be accurately aligned and allows forces introduced by the coil spring to be distributed over the support assembly. The receiving element may be produced from a rigid or load-bearing moldable material, while the damping element may be made from an elastomeric, resilient, or otherwise vibration-damping material selected according to the intended application.

In the installed state, the end of the coil spring is supported by the annular receiving element and is brought into direct or functionally effective contact with the damping element. Loads from the spring are therefore carried by the receiving element, while vibrations and shocks are attenuated by the damping element. The resulting one-piece or permanently integrated assembly combines secure spring support, reliable positioning, and effective damping in a compact component that is economical to manufacture and straightforward to install.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, saying “the book” suggests a particular book that the speaker and listener already know about.

Although “the” may seem simple, it adds clarity and precision to communication. It helps distinguish something familiar or unique from something general. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our solar system, while “a star” could refer to any star.

Used countless times in everyday speech and writing, “the” demonstrates how even the shortest words can play a vital role in language.

# Description

## Technical field

The present disclosure relates to a spring support, in particular to a spring support for supporting an end portion of a helical spring in a vehicle suspension system. The disclosure further relates to a method for manufacturing such a spring support by insert moulding an annular receiving element onto a damping element.

## Background

Spring supports are generally arranged between a helical spring and a spring seat or another component of a suspension assembly. A spring support may serve to locate the spring, transmit spring forces and reduce the transmission of noise and vibration.

Known spring supports may comprise a resilient damping part and a comparatively rigid reinforcing or receiving part. However, relative displacement between these parts, insufficient retention of the spring, and complicated assembly may reduce the durability or dimensional accuracy of the support.

It is therefore desirable to provide a spring support having a receiving element which is reliably connected to a damping element and which defines a stable spring-receiving geometry. It is additionally desirable to manufacture the spring support with a reduced number of assembly operations.

## Summary of the disclosure

According to a first aspect, a spring support comprises a damping element and an annular receiving element. The damping element is formed from an elastically deformable material and extends around a central axis. The annular receiving element is formed from a material having a greater rigidity than the material of the damping element and is insert moulded onto the damping element.

The receiving element comprises an annular support portion and a collar extending from the support portion. The collar is bent relative to the support portion and extends at least partially around the central axis. The support portion and the collar together define a receiving region for an end turn of a spring.

The bent collar may form a radially inner or radially outer boundary of the receiving region. In particular, the collar may be bent out of a plane of the annular support portion such that the collar has an axial extent. The transition between the support portion and the collar may be curved to avoid a sharp edge and to distribute stresses introduced by the spring.

The damping element may comprise an annular base body and at least one damping section projecting axially from the base body. The damping section may be positioned in the receiving region so that, in use, the spring bears directly against the damping element while the receiving element supports and geometrically stabilises the damping element.

According to a second aspect, a method for manufacturing the spring support comprises:

1. providing the damping element;
2. positioning the damping element in a mould;
3. closing the mould such that a cavity defining the annular receiving element is formed adjacent to at least one surface of the damping element;
4. introducing a mouldable material into the cavity;
5. forming the annular support portion and the bent collar of the receiving element in the cavity, with the receiving element being moulded directly onto the damping element;
6. solidifying the mouldable material; and
7. removing the resulting spring support from the mould.

The receiving element is thus formed after the damping element has been produced and positioned as an insert. The insert-moulding operation establishes a positive, frictional and/or material bond between the receiving element and the damping element without requiring a separate mechanical assembly operation.

## Brief description of the drawings

Exemplary embodiments are described below with reference to schematic drawings, in which:

**Figure 1** is a perspective view of a spring support;

**Figure 2** is a plan view of the spring support;

**Figure 3** is a sectional view along a radial plane through the spring support;

**Figure 4** is an enlarged sectional view of a receiving region and a bent collar; and

**Figures 5A to 5D** schematically illustrate successive manufacturing steps.

## Detailed description

A spring support 1 comprises a damping element 10 and an annular receiving element 20. The spring support 1 is centred on a central axis A. References to axial, radial and circumferential directions relate to the central axis A unless stated otherwise.

### Damping element

The damping element 10 comprises an annular base body 11 having a central opening 12. The base body 11 may be continuous in the circumferential direction or may include one or more interruptions, slots or recesses for drainage, deformation control or alignment.

The damping element 10 has a first axial side 13 facing a spring in an installed condition and an opposite second axial side 14 facing a spring seat. A damping section 15 is provided on the first axial side 13. The damping section 15 defines an annular or partially annular spring-contacting surface 16 against which an end turn of the spring is supportable.

The spring-contacting surface 16 may be inclined relative to a plane perpendicular to the central axis A. The inclination may vary in the circumferential direction so that the spring-contacting surface 16 follows the pitch of the end turn. In one embodiment, the axial thickness of the damping section 15 progressively increases along at least part of the circumference.

An end-stop formation 17 may be provided to determine the circumferential position of the terminal end of the spring. The end-stop formation 17 may be integral with the base body 11 and may comprise a shoulder extending radially and/or axially into the path of the end turn.

The damping element 10 is preferably formed from an elastomeric material, for example natural rubber, synthetic rubber, thermoplastic elastomer, polyurethane or a combination thereof. Voids, ribs or local variations in thickness may be provided to adjust the axial and radial stiffness of the damping element 10.

### Annular receiving element

The receiving element 20 extends circumferentially around the central opening 12 and comprises an annular support portion 21. The support portion 21 may have a substantially planar, frustoconical or circumferentially profiled geometry. In cross-section, the support portion 21 extends predominantly in the radial direction.

The support portion 21 is at least partially embedded in, or lies directly against, the damping element 10. A first surface 22 of the support portion 21 faces the damping section 15, while an opposite second surface 23 may remain exposed or may be covered by a layer of the damping material.

The receiving element 20 further comprises a collar 24 adjoining a radial edge of the support portion 21. The collar 24 is bent relative to the support portion 21. The expression “bent” encompasses a collar formed by shaping a preform before insert moulding and a collar moulded directly with a curved or angled transition.

The collar 24 may extend from a radially inner edge 25 of the support portion 21. In this configuration, the collar 24 projects generally axially and forms an inner guide for the spring. Alternatively or additionally, a collar may extend from a radially outer edge 26 and form an outer guide.

The collar 24 and the support portion 21 define, in radial section, an approximately L-shaped, J-shaped or hook-shaped receiving geometry. A transition region 27 between the support portion 21 and the collar 24 preferably has a radius of curvature rather than an abrupt corner. The transition region 27 can thereby resist local deformation and reduce stress concentrations.

The collar 24 may extend parallel to the central axis A. Alternatively, the collar 24 may be inclined towards or away from the central axis A. A free edge 28 of the collar 24 may be curved, flared or bent away from the receiving region in order to facilitate insertion of the spring and avoid damage to a protective coating of the spring.

The support portion 21, the collar 24 and the damping section 15 together define a spring-receiving channel 30. The channel 30 is open in an axial direction and is bounded:

- axially by the spring-contacting surface 16;
- radially on one side by the collar 24; and
- radially on the other side by a shoulder 18 of the damping element 10 and/or a further part of the receiving element 20.

The radial width of the channel 30 is selected to receive the end turn with radial clearance or with slight resilient interference. During operation, the damping element 10 isolates vibration and prevents direct hard contact between the spring and the receiving element 20. The receiving element 20 stabilises the channel 30 and limits excessive radial expansion or displacement of the damping element 10.

The receiving element 20 may comprise one or more apertures 29 through which material of the damping element 10 extends. Such apertures 29 provide mechanical interlocking. The damping element 10 may also comprise undercuts, grooves or projections which are enclosed by the moulded receiving element 20.

The receiving element 20 may be formed from a thermoplastic material, a fibre-reinforced polymer or another mouldable material having greater rigidity than the damping element 10. Suitable materials include polyamide, polypropylene, polyoxymethylene and fibre-reinforced variants thereof. The receiving element 20 may alternatively include a metallic insert overmoulded with a polymeric material.

### Relationship between the elements

The receiving element 20 is moulded directly onto the previously formed damping element 10. Consequently, the interface 31 between the elements follows the moulded geometry of the damping element 10. The receiving element 20 may contact the damping element 10 along the support portion 21, the transition region 27 and at least part of the collar 24.

The damping element 10 may include an annular locating recess 19. During insert moulding, the mouldable material fills the locating recess 19 to form an annular anchoring rib 32 of the receiving element 20. The anchoring rib 32 opposes axial separation of the elements. Circumferentially spaced recesses or projections may additionally oppose rotation of the receiving element 20 relative to the damping element 10.

In an embodiment, an elastomeric covering portion 33 extends over the free edge 28 of the collar 24. The covering portion 33 shields the spring from direct contact with the comparatively rigid receiving element 20. Since the damping element 10 is produced before the receiving element 20, the covering portion 33 may be positioned in the mould so that the collar 24 is formed adjacent to, or partially enclosed by, the covering portion 33.

## Method of manufacture

The damping element 10 is first manufactured independently of the receiving element 20. The damping element 10 may be produced by injection moulding, compression moulding, transfer moulding or another elastomer-forming process. After moulding, the damping element 10 may be cooled, cured or vulcanised as required by the selected material.

The preformed damping element 10 is subsequently placed in an insert-moulding tool. Locating surfaces of the tool engage the central opening 12, the second axial side 14 and/or dedicated locating formations of the damping element 10. The locating surfaces establish the axial and radial position of the damping element 10 while avoiding excessive compression of the spring-contacting surface 16.

When the tool is closed, a mould cavity is defined along the damping element 10. The cavity includes:

- a substantially annular cavity section defining the support portion 21;
- an axially extending cavity section defining the collar 24; and
- a curved or angled cavity section defining the transition region 27.

The mouldable material for the receiving element 20 is then injected into the cavity. The material flows circumferentially around the damping element 10 and fills the cavity sections in communication with one another. Where apertures, recesses or undercuts are present, the injected material enters these formations and produces a mechanical interlock after solidification.

The gate or gates may be positioned so that the support portion 21 is filled before or together with the collar 24. For example, the material may be introduced at one or more circumferentially spaced positions into the cavity section for the support portion 21 and may thereafter flow into the cavity section for the collar 24. This filling sequence reduces the likelihood of incomplete formation of the thin collar and promotes a continuous transition between the support portion 21 and the collar 24.

In another embodiment, the material is introduced through an annular or multiple-point gate such that flow fronts advance around the circumference in a balanced manner. Venting may be provided adjacent to the free edge 28 of the collar 24.

The temperature and pressure of the insert-moulding process are selected so that the receiving material conforms to the surface of the damping element 10 without causing unacceptable deformation or degradation thereof. The surface of the damping element 10 may be cleaned, plasma-treated, primed or otherwise activated before insertion into the tool if a material bond is desired.

After the receiving material has solidified sufficiently, the mould is opened and the integrated spring support 1 is removed. Any gate residue or flash may then be removed. The resulting component comprises the preformed damping element 10 and the subsequently insert-moulded receiving element 20 as a unitary handling assembly.

The order of manufacture is significant in that the resilient damping element 10 is provided first and acts as an insert during formation of the receiving element 20. The annular receiving element 20, including the support portion 21 and the bent collar 24, is therefore generated in its final position relative to the spring-contacting surface 16. Separate fitting, bending or fastening of the receiving element 20 to the damping element 10 after moulding is not required.

## Variations

The receiving element 20 need not form a completely closed ring. It may include one or more circumferential gaps while remaining annular in the sense that it extends around a major part of the central axis A. Similarly, the collar 24 may be continuous or may comprise a plurality of circumferentially separated collar segments.

The collar 24 may be formed with a constant axial height or with a height varying around the circumference. A locally increased collar height may be provided near the end-stop formation 17, where radial forces from the spring may be greater.

A plurality of concentric collars may be provided. For example, an inner bent collar and an outer bent collar may cooperate with the support portion 21 to define a U-shaped receiving cross-section. At least one of the collars may be embedded partly in the damping element 10.

Features described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features of another embodiment, provided that the resulting combination is technically compatible. Reference signs serve only to facilitate understanding and do not limit the scope of protection.
